bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds allocated: ₹111cr (capex), ₹18cr (R&D), ₹36cr (Noumed debt repayment), ₹33cr (working capital), ₹28cr (corporate/general); focus on debt reduction, capacity expansion, and R&D; no dividend policy disclosed
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory delays in EU-GMP upgrades; execution risk in Adelaide facility commissioning (Q4FY27); currency volatility in AUD/NZD; customer concentration in Australian pharmacy chains; competition from global CDMOs; reliance on expiring patents for R&D pipeline; integration risks from recent acquisitions
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Noumed’s Australian CDMO business is underpinned by exclusive supply agreements with pharmacy chains — a rare, sticky revenue model in generics; the AUD 20M government grant for Adelaide facility is non-dilutive capital, reducing financial risk; SP Analytics’ 67-dossier pipeline is targeted at patent cliffs within 3 years, creating a high-probability launch runway
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Acquisition track record tabled: Unit III Bhongir Rs. 24 cr (FY22), Unit IV Bollaram Rs. 11 cr (FY23), Revat Laboratories Rs. 28 cr (FY24), Noumed Pharmaceuticals Rs. 129 cr for 74.64% (FY26); proposed FY27 — Saicriti Rs. 83.8 cr for 60% and Prathyak Rs. 15 cr for 60%. A five-point assessment framework is set out (strategic fit, new regulated-market access, portfolio diversification via dossiers, operational synergy, leverage of acquired approvals).
- Path to full ownership on the two proposed deals: Saicriti's residual 40% to be acquired after 3 years at 12x trailing earnings, part-settled via an SPL share swap with right of first refusal; Prathyak's residual 40% within 2 years at the same valuation as the initial 60% (~Rs. 12 cr), from internal accruals.
- Balance of the Saicriti project funded by 40% equity (Rs. 55.89 cr) from Saicriti's promoters plus Rs. 75.24 cr project debt on a 3-year moratorium and 7-year repayment.
- Capital discipline stated as: "FY27 remains the peak debt year, with deleveraging from FY28"; project debt of Rs. 75.24 crore at the new subsidiary; capital directed to "high-visibility, long-tenure opportunities".
- Adelaide funding: AUD 53 mn total planned capex, of which an AUD 20 mn grant received from the Federal Australian Government and AUD 40 mn invested in the project to date, with the balance from debt plus accruals; funding for the AUD 53 million programme is stated as complete.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Five manufacturing facilities in India across segregated streams — non-beta-lactam sterile injectables, penicillin dry powder, cephalosporins and oral solids — letting anti-infectives be made in substantial volume without risk to the non-beta-lactam lines.
- Global regulatory accreditations (GMP, WHO-GMP, TGA-Australia, PIC/S) qualify output for domestic, regulated and semi-regulated international customers and for CDMO work.
- More than 50% of revenue contracted under long-term agreements, across 15 exclusive supply agreements covering 526 SKUs.
- Ownership of the customer relationship in Australia and New Zealand through Noumed, which works directly with major pharmacy chains and also provides warehousing, distribution, regulatory support and pharmacovigilance services generating recurring fee income.
- End-to-end model from formulation and analytical development through dossier compilation, regulatory approval, manufacturing and distribution, allowing selected outsourced volumes to be transitioned into in-house manufacturing while retaining product registrations and customer relationships.
- Meaningful capacity headroom: network utilisation moved from 15% in FY 22-23 to 60% in FY 25-26, with headroom remaining at several sites.
- Regulatory groundwork converts to contracted revenue — 69 Philippines FDA dossier approvals preceded a four-year exclusive anti-TB purchase order from Pill Corp.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Market competition, new technologies and stringent patent laws — The MD&A Risks and Concerns section states the Company is no exception to competition from the market, new technologies and stringent patent laws, and says it has identified such risks and is trying to counter them over a period of time.
- Rising raw material input costs squeezing profitability — Management describes the continuous increase in raw material input costs as a challenge that increases the pressure on the profitability of the Company.
- Government policy, inflation and global slowdown — The outlook is qualified as reasonably good only subject to the effects of government policies, inflationary pressure and a general global slowdown, which management says is bound to affect the Company.
- Exposure to domestic and overseas economic conditions and regulatory change — The cautionary statement names economic conditions affecting the domestic market and the overseas markets in which the Company operates, and changes in Government regulation, as important factors that could make actual results differ materially.
- Single-segment concentration — Segment-wise analysis is stated to be not applicable under Accounting Standard 17 because there is only one segment, Pharmaceutical — the business has no reported segment diversification to absorb a sector-level shock.
- Rising borrowings alongside expansion — The ratio commentary notes the interest coverage ratio improved on higher operating profitability despite an increase in borrowings, and that operating margin declined marginally on increased operating and input costs associated with business expansion.
- Newly listed entity — corporate governance regime only recently applicable — The Practicing Company Secretary certifies that the equity shares were listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited only with effect from April 2, 2026, so Regulations 17 to 27 on Corporate Governance were not applicable during FY 2025-26; the Directors' Report also records that Secretarial Audit under Section 204 was not applicable during FY 2025-26.
- Execution and integration of newly formed subsidiaries — Three companies became subsidiaries during the year — Sai Parenterals PTE Limited, Noumed Pharmaceuticals PTY Limited and Noumed Pharmaceuticals Limited — adding entities that must be consolidated and managed.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: CDMO revenue surged 250% YoY in FY26; 456 TGA-Australia approvals; 143 approvals in other markets; 302 complex products across injectables, tablets, capsules, orals, sprays; Noumed contributes Rx and OTC access in Australia/NZ; 74.6% stake in Noumed consolidated from Nov 2025
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Two verticals on one platform: CDMO Products & Services at 63% of FY26 net revenue (deck-stated 355.6% CAGR over FY23-FY26) and Branded Generic Formulations at 37% (deck-stated 15.6% CAGR over FY23-FY26). The deck states no CDMO work is undertaken domestically — the entire contract book serves export markets.
- Export revenue rose from 3% of Revenue from Operations in FY23 to 63% in FY26 (16.3% in FY25); private-sector share of revenue rose from 39% in FY23 to 81% in FY26 "as tender exposure recedes".
- The Noumed platform: 74.64% of Noumed Pharmaceuticals (Australia and New Zealand) acquired for AUD 22 million (including a primary infusion of AUD 4.00 million), completed 12th Nov 2025, bringing 451+ TGA dossiers, pharmacy-chain relationships and last-mile commercialisation. Deck claims Noumed is "the only organisation in Australia offering the full turnkey solution to multinational pharmaceutical companies".
- Australian pharmacy structure is the stated moat: chains own the consumer brand but hold no registrations and do no manufacturing; Noumed holds the marketing authorisation, the inventory and the logistics. 2,900 of Australia's 5,500 pharmacies are covered by the Wesfarmers Health, EBOS and Sandoz (Chemist Warehouse) networks.
- Contracted international revenue named in the deck: AUD 202 mn over a 7.5-year exclusive OTC supply agreement in Australia through Noumed, effective 1 July 2026, at approximately AUD 27 mn per annum (plus a 3-year option); and USD 11 mn on a 4-year exclusive anti-tuberculosis contract in the Philippines (from June 2026).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group structure] Subsidiaries: Revat Laboratories (100%, domestic branded generics), SP Analytics (75%, group R&D), Sai Parenterals Pte Limited Singapore (100%, holding company for cross-border transactions), Noumed Pharmaceuticals Pty Limited Australia (74.64%) and Noumed Pharmaceuticals Limited New Zealand (100%). Saicriti Pharma and Prathyak Laboratories would be added at 60% each.
- [US entry] The Board approved incorporation of a US subsidiary to support the Company's preliminary evaluation of entering the US market.
- [Listing] Completed IPO in March 2026 with a primary fund raise of Rs. 285 crore; listed on 2 April 2026 on BSE and NSE.
- [FY27 guidance] The Company reiterates FY27 guidance of Rs. 750 crore revenue at an EBITDA margin of around 17%, with growth weighted towards H2; the deck frames FY27 as "Build", FY28 as "Monetise" and FY29-30 as "Scale".
- [Future project] Land allotted by the Telangana Government for an oncology biosimilars and mAb facility with a technology partner; groundwork begins after the current capex (FY27-28 onwards).
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Sai Parenterals develops, manufactures and supplies finished pharmaceutical formulations across injectables, liquid orals, solid orals and topicals, covering both established and specialised or complex formats on the same manufacturing platform. The business runs as three complementary growth engines: Branded Generic Formulations for domestic and semi-regulated markets, CDMO exports where the company handles product development, technology transfer and commercial manufacturing under long-term agreements, and the Noumed platform, which holds direct customer relationships with Australian and New Zealand pharmacy chains for private-label and prescription products. The operating model connects formulation and analytical R&D, dossier compilation, regulatory approval, manufacturing and distribution, serving domestic, regulated and semi-regulated markets.

- **Liquid Orals:** Syrups, Suspensions, Solutions

- **Topicals:** Ointments, Creams, Gels

outlook.body: Strong export-led growth outlook for FY27 and beyond, driven by CDMO contracts, new facility commissioning in Adelaide (Q4FY27), and R&D pipeline acceleration. Focus on expanding branded generics in international markets and enhancing margins through higher-value complex products.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Reach out to export markets through active participation in Exports Industry Trade Shows.
- Develop new products through proper research and development, which management identifies as the opportunity set in the pharmaceutical industry.
- Counter identified risks — market competition, new technologies and stringent patent laws — over a period of time.
- Introduce Human Resource Development activities for overall improvement of the team and induction of professional manpower.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The manufacturing network comprises five facilities in India with roughly 1,160 million units per annum of installed capacity across 1,14,540 square feet of manufacturing area: Unit I at Jeedimetla, Telangana (sterile non-beta-lactam injectables, GMP compliant); Unit II at Jeedimetla (sterile penicillin dry powder injections on segregated beta-lactam systems, WHO-GMP certified); Unit IV at Bollaram, Telangana (dedicated cephalosporin facility, WHO-GMP certified); Unit III at Bhongir, Telangana (general oral dosage forms, TGA-Australia and PIC/S accredited, and home to the Formulation R&D plant); and the Revat Unit at Ongole, Andhra Pradesh (high-volume oral solids, GMP certified), operated by wholly owned subsidiary Revat Laboratories Private Limited. Network utilisation has risen from 15% in FY 22-23 to 60% in FY 25-26, meaningful headroom remains at several sites, and the penicillin line at Unit II now runs close to full utilisation and is being upgraded for regulated-market export. Overseas, a manufacturing base is being established at Adelaide through majority-owned subsidiary Noumed Pharmaceuticals: the facility is under development and on track for completion by the fourth quarter of FY 26-27, will produce tablets, liquid orals and nasal sprays, and represents planned capital expenditure of AUD 53 million, or approximately ₹311 Crore, supported by an AUD 20 million Australian Government grant already disbursed, against which the facility is committed to creating 150 jobs by FY 26-27 and establishing sovereign pharmaceutical manufacturing capability in Australia. Beyond the current network, land has been allotted by the Government of Telangana for a future facility dedicated to oncology biosimilars and monoclonal antibodies. As the Adelaide facility is commissioned and Indian capacity expands, a portion of products currently sourced from third-party manufacturers can transition to Group manufacturing.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Outlook for the industry and consequently for the Company during the current financial year is described as reasonably good, subject to government policies, inflationary pressure and general global slowdown.
- Export markets are flagged as a good opportunity, with management expecting success in the coming years from its trade-show outreach.
- Continuous increase in raw material input costs is stated to increase the pressure on profitability.
- India's generic drug producers hold a strong position in the global supply chain, with bulk drugs about one-fifth of industry output and formulations the rest; the Indian pharmaceutical market is third largest by volume and thirteenth by value.
- Higher revenue from operations and better collections from the CDMO business are cited as the reason debtor turnover improved.
- Inventory has been increased as the business scales up.
- Operating margin declined marginally on increased operating and input costs associated with business expansion, while the Company continued to achieve higher revenue growth.
- Net worth rose substantially on capital infusion to attain the stated objects of the IPO, which management says strengthens the financial base and supports future business growth.

The company is leveraging its expanded capacity and R&D center to capture high-margin export opportunities in regulated markets with strong visibility from long-term contracts.

one-line thesis: Sai Parenterals is a vertically integrated Indian pharmaceutical player scaling its global CDMO platform through strategic acquisitions in Australia and New Zealand, backed by regulatory-approved manufacturing and a growing dossier pipeline. The company is leveraging its expanded capacity and R&D center to capture high-margin export opportunities in regulated markets with strong visibility from long-term contracts.
guidance / outlook: Strong export-led growth outlook for FY27 and beyond, driven by CDMO contracts, new facility commissioning in Adelaide (Q4FY27), and R&D pipeline acceleration. Focus on expanding branded generics in international markets and enhancing margins through higher-value complex products.
order book & pipeline: Exclusive long-term CDMO supply agreements with Australian pharmacy chains; multiple regulated-market product registrations under development; 67 dossiers in pipeline
segment / subsidiary detail: CDMO revenue surged 250% YoY in FY26; 456 TGA-Australia approvals; 143 approvals in other markets; 302 complex products across injectables, tablets, capsules, orals, sprays; Noumed contributes Rx and OTC access in Australia/NZ; 74.6% stake in Noumed consolidated from Nov 2025
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Asia, Middle East, Latin America via leveraged regulatory dossiers; potential for new product launches from SP Analytics R&D center; upside from two-shift operations at existing facilities; possible further acquisitions in regulated markets
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved from 20% (FY25) to 24% (Q4FY26); PAT margin improved from 10% to 12% (Q4FY26); cost efficiencies from scale, vertical integration, and CDMO mix shift; capex-driven capacity expansion expected to improve unit economics over time
capex / expansion: Total capex of ₹111 crore from IPO proceeds allocated to manufacturing upgrades (Units I, II, III, IV); ₹18 crore for SP Analytics R&D center; AUD 53 million (₹2,800+ crore) for Adelaide facility (AUD 20 million grant received); total capex FY26-27 exceeds ₹3,000 crore

risks & watch-items: Regulatory delays in EU-GMP upgrades; execution risk in Adelaide facility commissioning (Q4FY27); currency volatility in AUD/NZD; customer concentration in Australian pharmacy chains; competition from global CDMOs; reliance on expiring patents for R&D pipeline; integration risks from recent acquisitions
non-obvious takeaways: Noumed’s Australian CDMO business is underpinned by exclusive supply agreements with pharmacy chains — a rare, sticky revenue model in generics; the AUD 20M government grant for Adelaide facility is non-dilutive capital, reducing financial risk; SP Analytics’ 67-dossier pipeline is targeted at patent cliffs within 3 years, creating a high-probability launch runway

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: An integrated, IP-led pharmaceutical formulations platform spanning branded generics, CDMO exports and a direct Australia and New Zealand presence, built on five manufacturing facilities in India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sai Parenterals develops, manufactures and supplies finished pharmaceutical formulations across injectables, liquid orals, solid orals and topicals, covering both established and specialised or complex formats on the same manufacturing platform. The business runs as three complementary growth engines: Branded Generic Formulations for domestic and semi-regulated markets, CDMO exports where the company handles product development, technology transfer and commercial manufacturing under long-term agreements, and the Noumed platform, which holds direct customer relationships with Australian and New Zealand pharmacy chains for private-label and prescription products. The operating model connects formulation and analytical R&D, dossier compilation, regulatory approval, manufacturing and distribution, serving domestic, regulated and semi-regulated markets.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Outlook for the industry and consequently for the Company during the current financial year is described as reasonably good, subject to government policies, inflationary pressure and general global slowdown.
- Export markets are flagged as a good opportunity, with management expecting success in the coming years from its trade-show outreach.
- Continuous increase in raw material input costs is stated to increase the pressure on profitability.
- India's generic drug producers hold a strong position in the global supply chain, with bulk drugs about one-fifth of industry output and formulations the rest; the Indian pharmaceutical market is third largest by volume and thirteenth by value.
- Higher revenue from operations and better collections from the CDMO business are cited as the reason debtor turnover improved.
- Inventory has been increased as the business scales up.
- Operating margin declined marginally on increased operating and input costs associated with business expansion, while the Company continued to achieve higher revenue growth.
- Net worth rose substantially on capital infusion to attain the stated objects of the IPO, which management says strengthens the financial base and supports future business growth.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The manufacturing network comprises five facilities in India with roughly 1,160 million units per annum of installed capacity across 1,14,540 square feet of manufacturing area: Unit I at Jeedimetla, Telangana (sterile non-beta-lactam injectables, GMP compliant); Unit II at Jeedimetla (sterile penicillin dry powder injections on segregated beta-lactam systems, WHO-GMP certified); Unit IV at Bollaram, Telangana (dedicated cephalosporin facility, WHO-GMP certified); Unit III at Bhongir, Telangana (general oral dosage forms, TGA-Australia and PIC/S accredited, and home to the Formulation R&D plant); and the Revat Unit at Ongole, Andhra Pradesh (high-volume oral solids, GMP certified), operated by wholly owned subsidiary Revat Laboratories Private Limited. Network utilisation has risen from 15% in FY 22-23 to 60% in FY 25-26, meaningful headroom remains at several sites, and the penicillin line at Unit II now runs close to full utilisation and is being upgraded for regulated-market export. Overseas, a manufacturing base is being established at Adelaide through majority-owned subsidiary Noumed Pharmaceuticals: the facility is under development and on track for completion by the fourth quarter of FY 26-27, will produce tablets, liquid orals and nasal sprays, and represents planned capital expenditure of AUD 53 million, or approximately ₹311 Crore, supported by an AUD 20 million Australian Government grant already disbursed, against which the facility is committed to creating 150 jobs by FY 26-27 and establishing sovereign pharmaceutical manufacturing capability in Australia. Beyond the current network, land has been allotted by the Government of Telangana for a future facility dedicated to oncology biosimilars and monoclonal antibodies. As the Adelaide facility is commissioned and Indian capacity expands, a portion of products currently sourced from third-party manufacturers can transition to Group manufacturing.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Five manufacturing facilities in India across segregated streams — non-beta-lactam sterile injectables, penicillin dry powder, cephalosporins and oral solids — letting anti-infectives be made in substantial volume without risk to the non-beta-lactam lines.
- Global regulatory accreditations (GMP, WHO-GMP, TGA-Australia, PIC/S) qualify output for domestic, regulated and semi-regulated international customers and for CDMO work.
- More than 50% of revenue contracted under long-term agreements, across 15 exclusive supply agreements covering 526 SKUs.
- Ownership of the customer relationship in Australia and New Zealand through Noumed, which works directly with major pharmacy chains and also provides warehousing, distribution, regulatory support and pharmacovigilance services generating recurring fee income.
- End-to-end model from formulation and analytical development through dossier compilation, regulatory approval, manufacturing and distribution, allowing selected outsourced volumes to be transitioned into in-house manufacturing while retaining product registrations and customer relationships.
- Meaningful capacity headroom: network utilisation moved from 15% in FY 22-23 to 60% in FY 25-26, with headroom remaining at several sites.
- Regulatory groundwork converts to contracted revenue — 69 Philippines FDA dossier approvals preceded a four-year exclusive anti-TB purchase order from Pill Corp.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Regulatory delays in EU-GMP upgrades; execution risk in Adelaide facility commissioning (Q4FY27); currency volatility in AUD/NZD; customer concentration in Australian pharmacy chains; competition from global CDMOs; reliance on expiring patents for R&D pipeline; integration risks from recent acquisitions

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Noumed’s Australian CDMO business is underpinned by exclusive supply agreements with pharmacy chains — a rare, sticky revenue model in generics; the AUD 20M government grant for Adelaide facility is non-dilutive capital, reducing financial risk; SP Analytics’ 67-dossier pipeline is targeted at patent cliffs within 3 years, creating a high-probability launch runway

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Capacity expansion and upgradation of manufacturing facilities (Units I-IV) toward EU-GMP/PIC/S**
- **Establishment of a new R&D centre**
- **Repayment/prepayment of certain outstanding borrowings**
- **Repay bridge/term loan for Noumed acquisition via Sai Parenterals Pte**
- **Complete Noumed Australian factory**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Reach out to export markets through active participation in Exports Industry Trade Shows.
- Develop new products through proper research and development, which management identifies as the opportunity set in the pharmaceutical industry.
- Counter identified risks — market competition, new technologies and stringent patent laws — over a period of time.
- Introduce Human Resource Development activities for overall improvement of the team and induction of professional manpower.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group structure] Subsidiaries: Revat Laboratories (100%, domestic branded generics), SP Analytics (75%, group R&D), Sai Parenterals Pte Limited Singapore (100%, holding company for cross-border transactions), Noumed Pharmaceuticals Pty Limited Australia (74.64%) and Noumed Pharmaceuticals Limited New Zealand (100%). Saicriti Pharma and Prathyak Laboratories would be added at 60% each.
- [US entry] The Board approved incorporation of a US subsidiary to support the Company's preliminary evaluation of entering the US market.
- [Listing] Completed IPO in March 2026 with a primary fund raise of Rs. 285 crore; listed on 2 April 2026 on BSE and NSE.
- [FY27 guidance] The Company reiterates FY27 guidance of Rs. 750 crore revenue at an EBITDA margin of around 17%, with growth weighted towards H2; the deck frames FY27 as "Build", FY28 as "Monetise" and FY29-30 as "Scale".
- [Future project] Land allotted by the Telangana Government for an oncology biosimilars and mAb facility with a technology partner; groundwork begins after the current capex (FY27-28 onwards).

one-line thesis: Sai Parenterals is a vertically integrated Indian pharmaceutical player scaling its global CDMO platform through strategic acquisitions in Australia and New Zealand, backed by regulatory-approved manufacturing and a growing dossier pipeline. The company is leveraging its expanded capacity and R&D center to capture high-margin export opportunities in regulated markets with strong visibility from long-term contracts.
guidance / outlook: Strong export-led growth outlook for FY27 and beyond, driven by CDMO contracts, new facility commissioning in Adelaide (Q4FY27), and R&D pipeline acceleration. Focus on expanding branded generics in international markets and enhancing margins through higher-value complex products.
order book & pipeline: Exclusive long-term CDMO supply agreements with Australian pharmacy chains; multiple regulated-market product registrations under development; 67 dossiers in pipeline
segment / subsidiary detail: CDMO revenue surged 250% YoY in FY26; 456 TGA-Australia approvals; 143 approvals in other markets; 302 complex products across injectables, tablets, capsules, orals, sprays; Noumed contributes Rx and OTC access in Australia/NZ; 74.6% stake in Noumed consolidated from Nov 2025
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Asia, Middle East, Latin America via leveraged regulatory dossiers; potential for new product launches from SP Analytics R&D center; upside from two-shift operations at existing facilities; possible further acquisitions in regulated markets
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved from 20% (FY25) to 24% (Q4FY26); PAT margin improved from 10% to 12% (Q4FY26); cost efficiencies from scale, vertical integration, and CDMO mix shift; capex-driven capacity expansion expected to improve unit economics over time
capex / expansion: Total capex of ₹111 crore from IPO proceeds allocated to manufacturing upgrades (Units I, II, III, IV); ₹18 crore for SP Analytics R&D center; AUD 53 million (₹2,800+ crore) for Adelaide facility (AUD 20 million grant received); total capex FY26-27 exceeds ₹3,000 crore
capital allocation: IPO proceeds allocated: ₹111cr (capex), ₹18cr (R&D), ₹36cr (Noumed debt repayment), ₹33cr (working capital), ₹28cr (corporate/general); focus on debt reduction, capacity expansion, and R&D; no dividend policy disclosed

themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
